title: Mixed-Precision Routing Capacity Heatmap Q2 2028
body:
Purpose:
Quick-turn planning sheet to compare routing policies that mix precision levels (FP16, INT8, 4-bit) and batching targets across regions to optimize fleet throughput while bounding customer-visible quality regressions. This is a working model used to surface high-leverage routing knobs for Q3 capacity commitments.

Assumptions (short):
- Workload mix: 55% short-chat (<=128 tokens), 35% mid (128-512), 10% long (>512).
- Models: base-redwood-13b (FP16), opt-13b-int8 (INT8 tuned), rwd-70b-q4 (4-bit hybrid).
- Hardware fleet: A100-40GB (primary), H100-80GB (spot for high-throughput), Ampere-small (GPU-misc).
- Target max quality regression tolerance: <=2.5% relative metric (perplexity/QA F1 depending on route).
- Autoscaling headrooms: 10% burst reserve per region.

Sheet grid (rows = region x gpu x precision x batch):
Region | GPU | Precision | Batch size | Estimated throughput (tokens/s) | Req/s (@avg 64 tokens) | p50 latency (ms) | Quality delta (%) | Fleet Utilization (%) | Notes
APAC | A100 | FP16 | 8 | 1,200,000 | 195 | 45 | 0.0 | 68 | baseline
APAC | A100 | INT8 | 8 | 1,760,000 | 286 | 62 | -1.4 | 78 | good throughput uplift, small latency increase
APAC | A100 | Q4 | 8 | 2,080,000 | 338 | 78 | -2.1 | 85 | pushes quality close to tolerance for conversational route
APAC | H100 | INT8 | 16 | 3,600,000 | 937 | 54 | -0.9 | 72 | use for steady high-batch traffic
APAC | H100 | Q4 | 16 | 4,200,000 | 1,093 | 68 | -1.8 | 81 | recommended for embeddings-heavy jobs only
EU | A100 | FP16 | 8 | 1,150,000 | 187 | 47 | 0.0 | 63 | slightly lower seq length mix
EU | A100 | INT8 | 8 | 1,700,000 | 276 | 64 | -1.6 | 74 | good tradeoff for mid workload
EU | A100 | Q4 | 8 | 1,980,000 | 321 | 80 | -2.3 | 83 | borderline for QA-sensitive customers
EU | H100 | INT8 | 12 | 2,850,000 | 751 | 58 | -0.8 | 70 | prioritized for enterprise routes with SLA
US | A100 | FP16 | 8 | 1,300,000 | 211 | 42 | 0.0 | 70 | baseline, high chat volume
US | A100 | INT8 | 8 | 1,900,000 | 308 | 58 | -1.2 | 80 | best cost/throughput for standard routes
US | H100 | Q4 | 16 | 4,500,000 | 1,173 | 72 | -1.9 | 88 | high utilization but acceptable for background batch
US | Ampere-small | Q4 | 4 | 640,000 | 100 | 140 | -3.5 | 50 | quality too degraded for chat; earmark for experimental low-priority tasks

Derived insights:
- INT8 with moderate batch sizes (8-12) gives the largest throughput uplift with modest quality delta (~-1.0 to -1.6%), suitable for most mid-latency routes.
- 4-bit (Q4) yields highest throughput but frequently approaches or exceeds the 2.5% quality tolerance on QA/eval sets for mid/long contexts; limit to low-stakes or embedding routes.
- H100 provides headroom for larger batch sizes while keeping p50 latency competitive; use H100 for reserved enterprise pools and burst routing.
- APAC shows the highest marginal utilization when shifting to INT8/Q4 (delta +10-17% utilization), so regional capacity plan needs +15% headroom or delayed rollout.

Routing policy recommendations (practical):
1) Default route: FP16 on A100 for <=128 token chat (maintain quality), fall back to INT8 for queued completion when latency SLO allows.
2) Mid routes (128-512): serve on INT8 A100; if queue depth exceeds threshold and latency SLO permits batch=16, migrate to H100-INT8.
3) Embeddings and non-interactive scoring: Q4 on H100 where utilization < 85% and quality metric is embeddings cosine stability (observed delta <1%).
4) Canary: roll Q4 in EU embedding route with 2% traffic, monitor eval set drift daily for 7 days.

Risk matrix (top risks):
- Quality regressions for long-context QA under Q4 -> Mitigation: block Q4 for QA-tagged routes and add automatic rollback when eval metric delta >2.5%.
- Regional oversubscription (APAC) from naive global rollouts -> Mitigation: staged rollout with regional quotas and backpressure routing to US/EU.
- Latency SLO misses under spike when batching increases -> Mitigation: enforce max batch-size per latency-sensitive route and keep 10% burst reserve.

Quick sensitivity checks (formulas used):
- Req/s = (throughput tokens/s) / (avg tokens per request). We used avg tokens per request = 64 for conversions to req/s.
- Utilization estimate = (provisioned_tokens_capacity * 100) / regional_token_budget. (regional_token_budget pulled from capacity planner v2 snapshot)
- Quality delta measured on holdout eval set: (baseline_metric - quant_metric)/baseline_metric * 100

Action items (next 2 weeks):
- [Rina] Run 48-hour canary for EU-embeddings Q4 at 2% traffic; capture embedding drift and latency distributions (due 2028-06-27).
- [Omar] Add routing knob to console to cap regional Q4 traffic at 10% per route (PR due 2028-06-24).
- [Li] Update capacity forecast to include +15% APAC headroom if INT8 adoption >30% (deliverable: updated workbook 2028-06-28).
- [Priya] Create eval dashboard with automated alerts when quality delta >1.5% for any customer bucket (prototype by 2028-06-29).

Notes and open questions:
- We need more granular evals split by prompt archetype (instruction-following vs. conversational chitchat) to understand Q4 impact; current eval set may underrepresent system prompts.
- Consider a hybrid quant profile: FP16 prefix + Q4 decode for long-context to reduce KV cache impact — engineering feasibility TBD.
- Cost model: INT8 reduces per-token cost ~22% vs FP16 on A100; Q4 reduces ~35% but increases variance in quality. Update pricing simulation if adoption exceeds 20%.

Data provenance: throughput benchmarks from unit run deck (bench/throughput/June-2028), quality deltas from eval run results id run-2028-06-10-quant-eval, fleet capacity numbers from regional capacity snapshot (capacity/2028-06-01).

Appendix (short table: decision thresholds):
Threshold | Action
Quality delta > 2.5% | Disable quantized routing for affected route; require manual review
Regional util > 90% | Trigger emergency capacity procurement pipeline + redirect new traffic to other regions
p50 latency > 200ms | Reduce batch-size by half for affected route and re-evaluate

This sheet is intentionally compact; expand into a dedicated workbook for modeling counterfactuals if stakeholders want distribution-level sims rather than point estimates.
